text:
mira: Heads-up — running the CLI during onboarding is spamming users with 3 separate env-var warnings if they have both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ORG_KEY set. It's confusing for first-time users.

alex: Can you paste the exact output? I haven't seen that.

mira: Sure — repro below (quick paste):

export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_prod_abc
export REDWOOD_ORG_KEY=org_xyz
redwood-cli login --verify

CLI output:
WARNING: REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and will be used.
WARNING: REDWOOD_ORG_KEY is set — this will override project-scope keys.
WARNING: Multiple credentials found; falling back to interactive prompt.

Feels loud and contradictory. It both says one key will be used and then that it's falling back.

sam: Ugh. That's bad DX. We agreed on a deterministic discovery order in the auth spec: (1) command flag, (2) project env var REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY, (3) org env var REDWOOD_ORG_KEY, (4) global REDWOOD_API_KEY, (5) default credentials file. If CLI prints all matches rather than the effective choice, people freak out.

jordan: Agreed — two quick fixes: (A) make discovery deterministic and quiet, only emit one compact line like: "Using REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (project-scoped); set REDWOOD_API_KEY to override" with a link to docs, and (B) add a --verbose flag that prints the full table of discovered vars for advanced debugging.

mira: Love that. Also we should avoid leaking full key values in logs — current warnings show partial keys like sk_prod_abc in some SDKs. Never print any secret.

alex: I'll take a small PR: change the CLI logger to compute chosen_source then emit a single info-level message showing source name and scope (project/org/global), and move the multiple-warning behavior behind --verbose. Will add a unit test for env var precedence and an e2e smoke for login.

sam: Make sure to mirror this in node/python/go SDK CLIs and the sample apps we ship in /examples/onboarding. We want parity so docs and onboarding are consistent.

alex: Yep. Proposed PR text: "cli(auth): deterministic credential discovery + compact messaging
- Compute effective credential source and only log the chosen source by default
- Add --verbose to list all discovered credentials (without values)
- Do not print partial keys anywhere
- Add unit tests for precedence and small sample update to onboarding README"

jordan: Quick UX nit — include a tiny inline hint when project key is used: "project key used; to share creds across projects, set REDWOOD_ORG_KEY". Keeps support tickets down.

devex-bot: Created issue #2345 for "CLI: noisy credential discovery warnings" and linked this thread — https://redwood/issue/2345

mira: Perfect. alex — can you target this for the next patch release? Also add a changelog entry and a short blurb in the onboarding doc so new users aren't surprised.

alex: Yep — will open PR today and ping here.

mira: :thumbsup:
